title: adaptive tool hedging and result coalescing to improve multi-tool ergonomics and streaming stability
text:
adaptive tool hedging and result coalescing to improve multi-tool ergonomics and streaming stability

description:
Motivation: multi-tool and parallel tool-call patterns were exposing two frequent pain points: 1) wasted duplicate work when multiple upstream planners (or speculative hedges) invoked equivalent tools in flight, and 2) streaming clients observed inconsistent marker points when tool results were injected out-of-order. This PR introduces an adaptive hedging/hedge-coalescer in the runtime and ergonomic surface updates in the API layer to: (a) deduplicate in-flight tool invocations across a request scope, (b) allow controlled parallelism with per-tool retry windows and jittered retry backoff, and (c) coalesce results deterministically for structured output and streaming consumers. Key design points: - In-flight idempotency tokens: tool invocations now carry a scoped idempotency key (derived from model request id + normalized tool signature) so workers can detect duplicate intent and avoid duplicate external calls. - Hedging controller: at runtime we run a short speculative hedging policy for latency-sensitive calls (configurable per-route). Hedged calls are registered with the coalescer rather than executed as independent outputs. - Result coalescer: worker-level component collects first-success responses and merges secondary responses into metadata (latency info, fallback reasons) instead of double-injecting content. This preserves streaming handshake semantics and keeps the final structured output deterministic. - OpenAI compat layer: updated function-calling adapter to respect the new idempotency semantics and to map merged results into a single function_call entry (with a tool_call_history array in metadata). - SDK ergonomics: TypeScript and Python SDKs expose an optional callHint to opt-in to hedging/coalesce behavior and surface a stable injection ordering promise for streaming clients. Checklist: - [x] Runtime: implement hedging controller + coalescer (server/runtime/tool_coalescer.py) - [x] API: add callHint + callToken to OpenAI-compat function call payloads (api/openai_compat/func_call_adapter.py, sdk/ts/src/tool/call.ts, sdk/python/redwood/tooling.py) - [x] Tests: unit tests for dedupe logic, coalescer, and streaming markers - [x] Docs: describe behavior and configuration (docs/observability/tool-hedging.md) - [x] Backwards compat verification against existing function-calling tests Summary of changes (high level): - server/runtime/tool_coalescer.py: new coalescer and hedging flow, small internal state machine for lifecycle of hedged calls. - api/openai_compat/func_call_adapter.py: serialize callToken/callHint, map coalesced responses to function_call with call_history metadata. - sdk/ts/src/tool/call.ts: add optional callHint param, promise-based injection ordering helper for streaming clients. - sdk/python/redwood/tooling.py: mirror ergonomics and provide convenience wrapper for idempotency token generation. - docs/observability/tool-hedging.md: short explainer and diagrams for typical flows. Commits: - 7f4b2d3: introduce tool_coalescer + hedging controller (core runtime) - c102b9a: openai compat adapter changes, map call_history into function_call metadata - 9a8d01f: ts & py sdk ergonomics + tests - 11b2e6a: add unit tests for dedupe and coalescer, CI tweaks - 5b7c0f2: docs and release notes Draft testing notes: initial canary against internal perf-canary showed median P95 token latency improvement of 8% for poly-tool workloads and a 25% reduction in duplicate external API calls for hedged routes. CI summary: first run had a flaky test in streaming-marker.t — fixed by adding a small sync barrier in the coalescer; final CI run: all checks passing. Backwards compatibility: default behavior off; existing routes unchanged unless callHint is provided or route-level hedging is enabled in config. Migration notes: enabling hedging on highly stateful external tools is discouraged until tool implementations are idempotent or the caller supplies a dedupe key. Related Linear tickets: ENG-1427 (tool hedging prototype), ENG-1534 (streaming marker stability). Links: (internal) Linear ENG-1427, ENG-1534.

review_thread:
Maya Chen (reviewer): Looks good overall. A few nits around naming; can we rename 'callToken' -> 'callId' in the public SDK surface? Also request a unit test for the coalescer's race case.
Ravi Patel (author): Renamed callToken -> callId in SDK and adapter; added race condition unit test in tests/runtime/test_coalescer_race.py. PTAL.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Can you add an integration smoke test that simulates a streaming client receiving the streaming markers and final injection? The guardrail in streaming-marker.t fixed the flake but want an explicit scenario.
Ravi Patel: Added integration/streaming/tool_injection_smoke.test which runs against local test harness; CI included smoke run in the last job.
Sofia Martinez (approver): Verified perf canary numbers and that openai-compat tests still pass. Approving to merge once CI green.
CI Bot: All checks passed on rerun (build, unit-tests, integration-smoke).
